messages:
Maya Chen: heads up — quantized rdlv2-4bit bring-up failing a slice of our safety promptset after the dedupe pass, ~6% drop in pass rate. tagging @Liam @Eva for triage
Liam O'Connor: noted. which promptset exactly? full eval report link?
Maya Chen: /evals/rdlv2/2026-03-19/safety-dedup-variant.csv — I pushed the report to the eval dashboard, but quick summary: regression concentrated on short-prefix QA prompts that got deduped aggressively; the quantized kernel seems to hallucinate more on truncated context.
Eva Patel: hmm — dedupe probably removed near-duplicates that provided necessary context patterns. can we check sampling strata? were short-prefix examples over-pruned?
Maya Chen: yes, dedupe threshold was 0.8 Jaccard on token n-grams, used across all lengths. It removed ~12% of short prompts.
Carlos Ruiz: labeler capacity note: if we want to reintroduce samples for golden relabel, we need to bump the priority queue. current SLA is 48h, might take a week for full relabeling.
Sasha (QA): Can we do a focused golden refresh with a small stratified set (<1k examples) for fast smoke? re-eval pipeline can run in ~30m for that size.
Liam O'Connor: agree with Sasha. propose: 1) build a 1k stratified holdout that over-samples short-prefix QA and instruction-following prompts; 2) bypass dedupe for that holdout; 3) run quantized recipe A/B (4-bit PTQ vs 4-bit QAT-ish) and compare.
Maya Chen: plan sounds good. quick CLI to pull sample:
```bash
rd-curate sample 
  --source=prod-promptstore \\n  --filters=task:short_qa,length:<64 \\n  --strata=task,length,lang \\n  --size=1000 \\n  --output=curation/holdouts/rdlv2-shortqa-1k.csv
```
Eva Patel: for the golden labels, we should include a small "context-augmented" variant — append 1-2 benign context lines to simulate near-duplicate context that got removed. that will help detect whether the model relies on those cues.
Carlos Ruiz: created a priority label job in LabelQueue as `LDQ-2319` and set workers=10 for 72h. ETA for first 200 completed: ~18h.
AnnotateBot: LabelQueue LDQ-2319 created by Carlos Ruiz — 10 workers allocated. link: https://labelboard.internal/LDQ-2319
Sasha (QA): also request that eval includes token-level diff and top-k logprobs for the failing examples — helps us see if it's confidence collapse vs hallucination.
Liam O'Connor: good call. I'll add metrics in eval config: `token_diff`, `topk_logprobs`, `prefix_cache_miss_rate`.
Maya Chen: one more: can we snapshot the pre-dedupe sample (for audit) and attach to ticket? I don't want to lose traceability if we reverse dedupe rules.
Eva Patel: i'll export pre-dedupe sample to `s3://rd-curation/archives/rdlv2/pre-dedupe-20260319.tar.gz` and add manifest.
Carlos Ruiz: after we have relabeled 200 examples, let's run a quick sanity eval and if it improves >3% we can roll a temporary rollback of dedupe for short prefixes.
Sasha (QA): I'll own the quick sanity eval and post results to the thread.
Maya Chen: thanks everyone. timeline: holdout build + upload by EOD, label job starts now, sanity eval after 200 labels (~tomorrow morning). tagging @all for visibility :eyes: 
Liam O'Connor: FYI I'll also kick off a quant-recipe grid with seed variation (seed=42, 99, 2026) to check randomness sensitivity. small compute run queued.
AnnotateBot: Task update: quant-grid job `QGRID-88` queued by Liam O'Connor. Status: queued.
Sasha (QA): if sanity eval still fails, next steps: 1) minimal dedupe rollback, 2) try 4-bit hybrid quant kernels, 3) escalate to infra for kernel trace.
Maya Chen: noted. please paste quick links/results here as they come in. I'll open a short runbook for the rollback path so PMs are aware of risk. thanks!
